verdict.rationale: Consensus is built as an academic search engine. It searches over 200 million academic papers, analyzes full text including paywalled publisher papers, and traces every insight back to the original source. It also offers filters by study type and journal, plus a peer-reviewed-only option. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of corpus coverage and search quality (all evidence is vendor-authored).

support.subject: As a researcher, I can search scholarly literature and primary sources, not just the open web

citations.quote: It searches over 200 million academic papers and uses language models to help you find, understand, and synthesize the literature faster.
Think of Consensus as an AI-native alternative to Google Scholar with a more-refined corpus.
Consensus analyzes the full text, including paywalled papers from major publishers, so you can find the most relevant papers.
Every response includes citations, so you can trace each insight back to the original source.
Filters allow narrowing by study type (RCT, meta-analysis, systematic review, observational), publication year, journal, open-access status, and discipline.
pass `exclude_preprints=true` (MCP) or `excludePreprints=true` (REST API) to filter to peer-reviewed papers only.
